## Sweep rulings 2026-10-10 (NT harmonise sweep; binding, decided by the reviewer from the Greek)

- R1 Ναζωραῖος = "Nazorean" / „Nazorejský“ in every place (Matt 2:23; 26:71; Luke 18:37; John 18:5, 7; 19:19; Acts 2:22; 3:6; 4:10; 6:14; 22:8; 24:5; 26:9). Ναζαρηνός = "Nazarene" / „Nazaretský“ in every place (Mark 1:24; 10:47; 14:67; 16:6; Luke 4:34; 24:19). Two Greek words, two renderings; neither is "of Nazareth" (that is ἀπὸ Ναζαρέτ). One token form per word in both languages.
- R2 μένω = "abide" of persons and of what is in them; "remain" of things, bodies and bare staying in a place (John 7:9; 19:31; Acts 5:4 and the like). Note the verb once per chapter.
- R3 γεννάω: active of the father "beget"; passive "be born", but "be begotten" where the father or the begetting is in view (Matt 1:16, 20; John 1:13; 1 John). One word inside one passage.
- R4 πειράζω = "tempt" toward evil; "test" where someone is put to the proof (John 6:6; Acts 9:26; Rev 2:2, 10; 3:10 and the like) — "test", not "try". CZ „pokoušet“ · „zkoušet“.
- R5 σκάνδαλον = "stumbling block" / „kámen úrazu“ in every place, so that it is heard with σκανδαλίζω "make stumble"; not "offense". Keep πρόσκομμα apart ("stumbling").
- R6 ἑταῖρος = "companion" ("Companion," in address) / „příteli“ is φίλος, so CZ „druhu“. Withdraw "comrade".
- R7 σεληνιάζομαι CZ = „stižený měsícem“ (Matt 4:24; 17:15); „náměsíčný“ means a sleepwalker today. EN "moonstruck" stays.
- R8 Matt 16:22 Ἵλεώς σοι = "Far be it from you, Lord!" / „Buď toho ušetřen, Pane!“ (no "God" supplied). The Greek is a set phrase of refusal; the word-for-word "Propitious to you" goes to Changes (as with the oath formula).
- R9 ἐπιστάτης: EN "Chief" stays; CZ = „Mistře“ (not „Náčelníku“).
- R10 στέφανος CZ = „věnec“ everywhere (also Jas 1:12; 1 Pet 5:4). φωνὴ μεγάλη CZ = „veliký hlas“ everywhere (also Rev 12). CZ γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν = „Zplozenci zmijí“ (also Matt 3:7). ποιέω καρπόν = "make fruit" (also Matt 3:8, 10). χιλίαρχος = "chiliarch" / „velitel tisíce“ (also Mark 6:21). διατάσσω of an everyday order = "give orders" (also Acts 23:31).
- R11 No change: ὅσιος "holy" of God (Rev 15:4; 16:5); χλωρός "pale" of the horse (Rev 6:8); δεῖ "must / it is necessary"; ἐκδικέω "avenge"; φιμόω "muzzle".
- R12 OPEN POLICY closed: tokens whose original form is the Hebrew name of the same person or place (Yahweh for κύριος in an Old Testament quotation, Sea of Reeds, Perat, Har Megiddo, Gulgolta, Beit Zata) stay. That is the design of the "original" mode: the Hebrew name of the one named; the Greek form is given in Changes wherever it differs.
- R13 παραδίδωμι: "deliver up" / „vydat“ whenever a person (or oneself, a soul) is handed into another power or to death — also Rom 1:24, 26, 28; 4:25; 8:32; Gal 2:20; Eph 4:19; 5:2, 25; Acts 15:26 (not "give up"). "deliver" / „předat“ of a tradition or teaching (Luke 1:2; 1 Cor 11:2, 23; 15:3; 2 Pet 2:21; Jude 3). "give over" / „svěřit“ to grace (Acts 14:26; 15:40). No "hand over", no "betray".
- R14 ναός = "sanctuary" / „svatyně“ in every book; ἱερόν = "temple" / „chrám“. Two Greek words, two renderings (John 2:19–21; Matt 23:16–35; 26:61; 27:5, 40, 51; 1 Cor 3:16–17; 6:19; 2 Cor 6:16; Eph 2:21; 2 Thess 2:4 and the rest).
- R15 ἐρωτάω: "ask" of a question; "request" / „žádat“ of asking for something (one word; not "make request", not "ask"), so that it stays apart from αἰτέω "ask" / „prosit“.
- R16 φιλέω = "have affection for" / „mít rád“ in every place (also Rev 22:15; Matt 6:5; 10:37; 23:6; Luke 20:46; John 5:20; 16:27; 1 Cor 16:22; Titus 3:15); "kiss" / „políbit“ only of the kiss.
- R17 ἐπιμένω = "remain" ("remain in / on") / „zůstat“ in every place; not "abide", which is μένω of persons.
- R18 CZ βλασφημέω: „rouhat se“ (+ dative) when God, his name, the Spirit or what is God's is the object or no object stands; „tupit“ when a man or a thing of men is the object. EN "blaspheme" in both.
- R19 CZ κράτος = „síla“; only where ἰσχύς stands beside it (Eph 1:19; 6:10; 1 Pet 4:11) κράτος is „mohutnost“. Czech has no third word; note it in Změny. (δύναμις „moc“, ἰσχύς „síla“.)
- R20 CZ σπουδάζω = „usilovat“. CZ ὁδηγός = „průvodce“ („vůdce“ is ἡγούμενος / καθηγητής). CZ δωρεάν = „zdarma“ (John 15:25 „bez příčiny“ is another sense and stays). φορτίον = "load" / „náklad“ in every place (also Matt 11:30; 23:4; Luke 11:46), βάρος = "burden" / „břemeno“.
- R21 No change: λαμβάνω CZ „dostat“ (a thing) · „přijmout“ (a person, or willingly) · „vzít“ (take) are three senses of the one verb.
